A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DISCO, with the same authors and central scoring method. All 23 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reorganization and retitling.

before.justification: V1 reports original CVI comparisons, clustering experiments, sensitivity analyses and noise-label evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds runtime measurements, DBCV parameter-selection studies, noise-distribution experiments and evaluations on six additional real-world datasets.

M1.justification: The density-connectivity distance, pointwise cluster score, minimum of the sparsity and distance noise scores, aggregation and edge-case rules remain unchanged. V1's Equations (2)-(9) correspond to v2's Equations (1)-(8); renaming and reorganized explanations do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: V2 adds cluto-t5-8k and noise-label evaluations on Iris, Seeds, WiFi, Spambase, Wine quality and Yeast. It also tests Gaussian and Poisson noise alongside uniform noise. The original 19-dataset benchmark inventory remains, but several earlier synthetic scenarios and the zelnik4 case study disappear.

E2.justification: MMJ-SC is added as an evaluated comparator in Tables 2, 3 and 4, and in the new runtime comparison. The other principal CVI comparators remain. This adds a relevant comparison method without replacing the comparator family.

E3.justification: Table 4 changes from ten labelings to seven, dropping DPC, Spectral Clustering and MeanShift outputs. V2 withholds PCC when any evaluation fails instead of reporting partial coverage. Table 3 changes CVDD's reported noise treatment from an additional cluster to filtering. New experiments introduce DBSCAN parameter grids and individual cluster-point relabeling procedures.

E4.justification: V2 adds benchmark-wide hyperparameter sweeps, noise-distribution tests, real-data relabeling analyses and DBCV selection-instability studies. It removes v1's line-cluster, density-ratio, random-cluster-count, added-dimension and degenerate-data analyses. The three cluster-score sensitivity tests are retained in Appendix D.6, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V1's general ten-run averaging disclosures, benchmark standard deviations and random-label confidence band disappear. V2 adds separate 100-shuffle DBCV studies with means, ± summaries and selection frequencies in Tables 5 and 6, but leaves repeat counts for the revised main comparisons unspecified. This does not establish an overall increase or decrease in runs performed.

E6.justification: Numerous reported results change: for example, Table 2's DBCV score for complex9 ground truth changes from 0.17 to -0.15. Table 3 replaces the noise examples, and Table 4 reports replacement correlations under a different design, not same-setting gains. V2 adds runtime and new noise-study results while removing v1's detailed benchmark and DISCO/ARI tables.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix A's arguments establishing determinism and boundedness, detailed computational-complexity derivation and linear-space reasoning are removed. V2 retains assertions of determinism, boundedness and O(n²) complexity without those derivations. The central mathematical definitions remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a pointwise density-based CVI that explicitly evaluates noise labels. V2 removes the abstract's broad claim that experiments show more consistent evaluation than competitors, emphasizing instead explicit noise assessment, the Silhouette foundation and coverage of edge cases.

C2.justification: V2 develops the practical implications of DBCV variability for parameter selection, explains large-µ sensitivity on 3-spiral and COIL20, and interprets negative noise scores as HDBSCAN overassigning noise. It removes substantial discussion of alternative noise notions, subspace extensions and evaluation biases from v1 Appendix D.

D1.justification: V2 documents new experimental details, including the DBSCAN grid, Poisson parameter and HDBSCAN defaults, and adds a reproducibility statement. The anonymous repository identifier changes from DISCO-8E44 to DISCO-E358. Hardware, preprocessing and most CVI defaults remain, while v1's efficient traversal and linear-space implementation guidance disappears.

R1.justification: V2 adds MMJ-SC, FairDen and dataset-source citations, while removing references associated with SHADE, SCAR, subspace evaluation and several deleted discussions. It more explicitly positions DISCO as a Silhouette-based extension with noise evaluation, while retaining its overall relationship to density-based CVIs.

P1.justification: The title, acronym expansion, abstract and introductory narrative are revised. Method subsections are consolidated, experimental sections are reorganized, and the appendices receive a substantially different structure. Reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figures 3 and 4 of v1 move to the appendix, the cluster-score ablation is enlarged and gains dataset illustrations, and parameter-selection plots are merged. New experimental displays replace many earlier appendix figures and tables; Table 4 also loses its coverage-percentage display.

improvement.justification: The MMJ-SC comparison, noise tests on real datasets, distributional checks and runtime measurements strengthen empirical validation. However, v2 removes the raw DISCO/ARI table and general repeated-run disclosures while substantially revising the correlation protocol, making the central comparisons harder to audit. Together with the loss of the detailed complexity argument, these material tradeoffs prevent a reliable judgment of net improvement.
